review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the repo for uses of decodedLeading, decodePool, actualPool and nextPrefixDecoder. I read GeometricValues.lean, which uses decodedLeading three times. The CW75 variant uses it the same way. The only well-supported simp-interface issue is that decodedLeading has no unfolding or apply lemma. The file has no simp attributes. The other definitions (decodePool, nextPrefixDecoder, actualPool) have no uses outside this file that would justify a simp lemma, so I did not recommend annotations for them. I could not run Lean. The suggested lemma is untested, and its statement needs checking against the Decidable instance that `classical` and the `ite` produce.

findings.problem: decodedLeading is a tactic-built definition (`by classical exact fun x y z => if ...`) with no pointwise evaluation lemma. Every consumer has to run `unfold decodedLeading` or `simp [decodedLeading, ...]`. Inside the file this is `simp [decodedLeading, h]` in surviving_nextPrefix and `unfold ... decodedLeading` in rawPoolLeading_eq_decodedLeading. Downstream, GeometricValues.lean (raw_XY_normal, raw_XZ_normal, raw_YZ_normal) and the matching CW75ReorderedGeometricValues.lean theorems call `unfold decodedLeading` and then `simp only [...]` on the exposed `ite`. The unfolded form is a raw `fun x y z => if ...` that depends on the `classical` decidability instance. Each user must expose it by hand, and the guard form is not fixed in one place.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma that fixes the normal form, e.g. `theorem decodedLeading_apply (pool counts fine p x y z) : decodedLeading pool k counts fine p x y z = if x.2.1 = y.2.1 ∧ x.2.1 = z.2.1 ∧ decodePool pool k counts p x.2.1 = fine p x.1 y.1 z.1 ∧ x.2.2 = y.2.2 then 1 else 0 := by classical unfold decodedLeading; rfl` (the decidability instance may need care). Mark it `@[simp]`, or at least use it in `simp only [decodedLeading_apply]`. Keep `decodedLeading` itself opaque to simp. Then replace the `unfold decodedLeading` calls (here and in the Completion and CW75 GeometricValues files) with this lemma.
findings.benefit: The guard shape is stated once instead of being re-exposed with `unfold` in at least six places. `simp` can evaluate decodedLeading directly, as in the `by simp [decodedLeading, h]` step. The downstream `*_normal` proofs no longer depend on the internal `by classical exact fun` definition, so they will not break if its decidability instance changes.
